title: Prove campaign rules and ambiguity resolution end to end
description:
Objective
Add end-to-end tests that prove campaign-rule behavior across persistence, model context, audit, ambiguity resolution, accepted-turn commits, and immediate disputed-turn replay.

Required scenarios
1. Create Undead explicit ambiguity question prompts without invented certainty and persists an approved interpretation.
2. Create Undead mixed ghast/wight action establishes visible mixed-within-total precedent only after DM/auditor acceptance.
3. Find Familiar permanent-dismissal-after-0-HP ambiguity prompts and remains unresolved when no choice is approved.
4. Explicit "no material components" house rule is durable prose.
5. Immediate material-components objection applies from disputed-turn start, restores pre-turn state, replays, and makes replay canonical.
6. Ordinary house-rule creation applies prospectively.
7. Supersession and revocation change active sets without mutating history.
8. DM and auditor receive equivalent active rule sets at every tested position.
9. Ordinary contextual adjudication (cover/visibility/terrain suitability) creates no campaign rule.
10. A clear canonical-rule violation never becomes an implicit house rule.

Architecture and references
Exercise the public/runtime path built by eshyra-jhpt.1-.8 and PR #419 RulesAmbiguity metadata from eshyra-o9bd.18.7.9. Assert immutable pack bytes remain unchanged and campaign prose remains in canonical campaign history.

Non-goals
No live-provider tests as the sole proof; no duplicated full ambiguity registry; no arbitrary retrospective history editing; no selective-retrieval optimization benchmark; no deterministic interpretation of arbitrary house-rule prose.
acceptance_criteria:
All ten scenarios pass through realistic campaign turn/context/audit/storage boundaries; tests prove exact DM/auditor rule-set parity, checkpoint/replay timing, accepted-vs-abandoned canon, pack immutability, and no rule creation for contextual judgments or clear canonical violations; full repository verification passes.

ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT (integrated transition design section 8.3, A3 and
A4; accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8, PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). Three of the ten scenarios must be
provable end to end as an explicit triple, because they are the three cases the
transition's campaign-rule probes consume:

1. UNRESOLVED AMBIGUITY - a discovered RulesAmbiguity with no active ruling keeps
   its published uncertainty, surfaces the known interpretations, and never
   acquires silent canonical certainty (existing scenarios 1 and 3).
2. RESOLVED RULING - an approved interpretation becomes a durable prose ruling
   carrying ambiguity ID, interpretation ID, kind, status, provenance, effective
   position, and supersession status, and is supplied on subsequent turns
   (existing scenarios 1 and 2).
3. NON-AMBIGUITY HOUSE RULE - the "no material components" house rule, an
   intentional override of clear canonical behavior with no underlying source
   ambiguity, is durable prose that coexists with the source material it
   overrides rather than replacing or hiding it (existing scenarios 4 and 5).

Scenario 9 (ordinary contextual adjudication creates no campaign rule) is not
weakened by any of this and remains a required negative.

Additionally, the accepted-turn trace evidence required by amendment A3 on
eshyra-jhpt.4 - which active rules and rulings were supplied for the turn, and
under which identities - must be proven end to end here, from the persisted
trace, without a second campaign-rule store or a parallel audit database.

These three cases are what eshyra-o9bd.19.13 (transition W11) consumes for probes
P7 (cube-of-force ambiguity, both the unresolved and the resolved case) and P10
(the material-components house rule). W11 depends on these outputs and may not
substitute a discovery-local rule or ruling store; campaign-rule persistence and
ruling lifecycle remain owned by eshyra-jhpt.
